title: Cohort-Driven Quarterly Runbook: Scenario Roadmaps for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Lina Chen
description: Create a practical, scenario-based quarterly runbook that maps cohorts, release lanes, and rollback signals for the Hosted API and model catalog. Purpose is to give PMs, Eng, and Design a single source-of-truth for which customer cohorts get which model variants when, and what operational signals will trigger rollbacks or slow-rolls. This ticket covers OKR alignment, milestone calendar, cross-team dependencies, and a lightweight playbook for canaries and capacity hedges.
objectives: Map runbook to Q2 OKRs: 1) reduce 95th percentile latency by 10% for hosted endpoints; 2) maintain model-quality regression <0.5% across rotations; 3) reduce per-token cost for top-3 endpoints by 8% through caching/quantization guidance
Define three delivery cohorts (Beta, Expansion, GA) and criteria for moving cohorts between lanes
Provide an operations checklist and rollback decision tree for staged model swaps and capacity incidents
acceptance_criteria: Runbook final doc published in Confluence and linked here
Stakeholder sign-offs from Eng, SRE, Design, Sales, and CS recorded in comments
Automated canary dashboard (per-cohort) created with p50/p95 latency, error-rate, unit-cost, and quality-regression signal panels
A gated checklist added to model deployment pipeline that enforces cohort boundaries and fallback rules

metrics: Latency target: p50 -5% / p95 -10% baseline vs 2026-02; monitored per-cohort
Quality target: model output regression <=0.5% on eval prompt set (daily check)
Cost target: unit token cost reduction >=8% for top-3 endpoints (monthly measurement)
Availability SLO: 99.9% per endpoint during rollout windows
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Prioritize latency improvements for Tier-1 endpoints in Beta cohort; cost optimizations will be staged for Expansion cohort to avoid introducing regression risk
Decision: Rollbacks are allowed for any cohort if quality regression >0.7% OR p95 latency degradation >25% over 15 minutes (decision made 2026-03-04)
Trade-off: Using more aggressive quantization for Expansion cohort may increase hallucination risk; mitigations: run targeted evals and enable defensive prompting
runbook_steps: 1) Pre-roll: Validate model artifact and quantization profile, run baseline eval suite, generate canary config
2) Canary: Enable model for Beta cohort (1-2% traffic) for 24h, monitor dashboard signals and manual QA samples
3) Slow-roll: If canary OK, expand to Expansion cohort (10-20% traffic) with 48-72h observation window
4) GA: Full rollout to GA cohort after automated checks and stakeholder sign-off
5) Fallback: If rollback triggers hit, instantly route cohorts to previous stable variant and open incident; postmortem within 72h
